title: Thematic Anchor Grid and Constraint Playbook for Responsive Console Tokens
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a compact, thematically anchored token and component playbook to standardize responsive density, contrast, and rollout affordances across console dashboards and cost views. Goal is to reduce visual drift between pages (Cost Explorer, Rollouts, Model Metrics) and provide a migration path for older panels. Deliverables: 1) Figma library update with anchor-grid token set and interactive component variants, 2) Accessibility contrast targets and test checklist, 3) Migration checklist and developer API notes for Rollout Controls and Cost Sparkline components.

Scope and constraints:
- Must work within current Console layout breakpoints (xs, sm, md, lg) without breaking legacy compact pages.
- Tokens should map to runtime props used by frontend components (density, tone, emphasis, elevation).
- Maintain existing cost card width/height ratios for enterprise dashboards to avoid data jitter during rollout.
- Prioritize text and UI contrast targets to meet AA for body text and AAA where possible for small numeric values.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Single canonical token set with responsive scaling factors. Pros: single source of truth; Cons: may force rework in older pages.
- Option B: Anchor-grid tokens (preferred): small set of anchors (compact / default / spacious) with constrained interpolation rules giving components room to opt into exact anchors. Pros: easier incremental migration; Cons: slightly more mapping logic in component APIs.
- Decision: Adopt Anchor-grid tokens + migration shim in CSS variables to allow older pages to opt-in via a data attribute.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma library published with Anchor Grid tokens and 12 component variants (cards, rails, metric chips, sparklines, rollout rail).
- Accessibility checklist passed in internal QA lab for 3 core console pages.
- Frontend engineers able to consume tokens via CSS variables + React design tokens package.

Migration plan (high level):
1) Publish Figma tokens and component variants; share walkthrough with Eng and PM.
2) Implement token-to-CSS-variable shim in design-token repo (engineering task).
3) Migrate Cost Explorer card -> set data-anchor="compact" then test.
4) Rollout in waves: internal pages -> beta customers -> default.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/console-anchor-grid-prototype
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Anchor+Grid+Playbook
- Design tokens repo issue: ENG-70211 (dependency)
- Draft QA checklist: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/placeholder

Notes on component API changes (for engineers):
- New prop: anchor (string) values: compact | default | spacious. Maps to token anchors.
- New data attribute for legacy pages: data-token-phase=shim-anchors to apply CSS variable fallback.
- Suggest small migration helper util in react-design-tokens: mapOldSpacingToAnchor(oldSpacing)

Testing and validation plan:
- Usability microtest with 6 product engineers to validate perceived density and affordance for rollout controls (3/10–3/12).
- Automated visual diff in storybook per variant. Threshold: 0.8 SSIM for major changes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: consumer components differ in how they apply elevation and shadows causing token misalignment. Mitigation: publish shadow token guide and require shadow token audit during PR reviews.
- Risk: accessibility regressions for small numeric types in cost cards. Mitigation: enforce numeric token with higher contrast; run contrast-check tool in CI.
